newsitem.title: ISRAEL: El Al talking about Airbus planes.
newsitem.headline: El Al talking about Airbus planes.

text.p: El Al Israel Airlines begins talks on Monday with a visiting Airbus delegation on the purchase of five aircraft in a deal worth more than $200 million, a spokesman for the state-owned carrier said.
"We are seeking five planes in the 125-150 seat range and they want to show us what they have to offer," spokesman Nachman Kleiman told Reuters.
Kleiman said El Al would look at Airbus Industrie's short- to medium-range A-319 and A-320 airplanes.

A deal with the European consortium would mark a departure for the Israeli carrier, whose entire current 28-plane fleet was supplied by Seattle-based Boeing Co. El Al will take delivery of a 29th plane, a Boeing 747-400, in 1999.
"If a deal is achieved with Airbus obviously it would be a break from the past," Kleiman said.
He said El Al sought to replace some older Boeing model 737s and 757s and had not ruled out a deal with the U.S. company.
"We are interested in either purchasing or leasing and obviously we are willing to listen to offers."
Kleiman said the five-aircraft deal worth upwards of $200 million would be the company's largest purchase in years.
When asked whether the airline had a target date to make a decision on the purchase, Kleiman replied: "We'd like the airplanes to start entering our fleet in 1998."
